title: Monthly activity with missing months and growth
prompt: For every `[retail].[Customers]` row, return all twelve months of 2024, including months with no `Orders` rows. Use `OrderDate` for month boundaries and `OrderTotal` for totals. Return `CustomerID`, `CustomerName`, MonthStart, EventCount, KnownValueCount, TotalValue, PreviousMonthValue and GrowthPercent. A month with no rows has total zero; a month containing only unknown values has total NULL. Sum known values for mixed months. Growth is 100 * (current - previous) / previous; return NULL when either total is unknown, there is no previous month, or the previous total is zero. Partition LAG by the master key. Use a calendar CTE and order by `CustomerID`, MonthStart.
sql:
;WITH Months AS (
    SELECT CAST('20240101' AS date) AS MonthStart
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD(month, 1, MonthStart)
    FROM Months WHERE MonthStart < CAST('20241201' AS date)
), Activity AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(OrderDate), MONTH(OrderDate), 1) AS MonthStart,
           COUNT(*) AS EventCount, COUNT(OrderTotal) AS KnownValueCount,
           SUM(OrderTotal) AS TotalValue
    FROM [retail].[Orders]
    WHERE OrderDate >= '20240101' AND OrderDate < '20250101'
    GROUP BY CustomerID, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(OrderDate), MONTH(OrderDate), 1)
), Filled AS (
    SELECT p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName, m.MonthStart,
           COALESCE(a.EventCount, 0) AS EventCount,
           COALESCE(a.KnownValueCount, 0) AS KnownValueCount,
           CASE WHEN a.EventCount IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE a.TotalValue END AS TotalValue
    FROM [retail].[Customers] p CROSS JOIN Months m
    LEFT JOIN Activity a ON a.CustomerID = p.CustomerID AND a.MonthStart = m.MonthStart
), Compared AS (
    SELECT *, LAG(TotalValue) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY MonthStart) AS PreviousMonthValue
    FROM Filled
)
SELECT *, 100.0 * (TotalValue - PreviousMonthValue) / NULLIF(PreviousMonthValue, 0) AS GrowthPercent
FROM Compared
ORDER BY CustomerID, MonthStart

title: Consecutive active-date streaks
prompt: Find consecutive calendar-date streaks per `CustomerID` in `[retail].[Orders]` using `OrderDate`. Deduplicate same-day activity before using ROW_NUMBER and a gaps-and-islands grouping key. Return `CustomerID`, `CustomerName`, StreakStart, StreakEnd and ActiveDays for streaks of at least two days. Multiple rows on one date count as one active day. sql:
;WITH ActiveDates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID, OrderDate FROM [retail].[Orders]
), Numbered AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, OrderDate,
           DATEDIFF(day, '20000101', OrderDate)
           - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate) AS IslandKey
    FROM ActiveDates
), Streaks AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, MIN(OrderDate) AS StreakStart, MAX(OrderDate) AS StreakEnd, COUNT(*) AS ActiveDays
    FROM Numbered GROUP BY CustomerID, IslandKey HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

title: Trailing 30-calendar-day comparison

           AVG(CAST(priorRow.OrderTotal AS decimal(19,4))) AS PriorAverage

title: Consecutive active-date streaks

title: Trailing 30-calendar-day comparison

title: Monthly activity with missing months and growth

           CASE WHEN a.EventCount IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE a.TotalValue END AS TotalValue
    FROM [brokerage].[BrokerageAccounts] p CROSS JOIN Months m
    LEFT JOIN Activity a ON a.AccountID = p.AccountID AND a.MonthStart = m.MonthStart
), Compared AS (
    SELECT *, LAG(TotalValue) OVER (PARTITION BY AccountID ORDER BY MonthStart) AS PreviousMonthValue
    FROM Filled
